assessment_v11.method: Existing score_v11.py and audiences.json. No changes to schema or weights.
assessment_v11.note: These are evidence-based assessments, not numeric v1.1 outputs. The existing scorer requires mapped piste kilometres, POI counts, gradient, access and guide datasets. Published run counts are not substituted for mapped piste kilometres.

dimensions.assessment: Positive terrain breadth: 15 green and 26 blue runs, plus protected family and discovery areas. Quality of beginner terrain, drag share, flatness, ski school coverage and access remain to be measured.

Strong valley-wide family proposition. Protected family areas and discovery zones combine with pools, ice rink, dog sledding and indoor activities. The four-sector layout makes accommodation-to-lift convenience village-dependent.

Credible expert offer. Named guided routes include Tour du Prorel, La Balme Couloir, Tête des Grands Prés, Vallons des Corneilles and Vallons de la Montagnole. Published summit altitude is 2,800 m with 1,600 m vertical. Guide coverage, steep kilometres, glacier area and lift-reachable freeride kilometres remain to be measured.

Mixed. A 250 km domain and 26 blue plus 28 red runs provide scale; operator material identifies Big Air, snowboard cross and half-pipe/freeride features. Drag lift share and flat intermediate terrain are decisive in this recipe and cannot be inferred from run counts.

Freestyle features are identified across the sectors, including Big Air, snowboard cross and half-pipe/freeride. Current maintained park count and combined area are unverified. These carry most of the recipe weight and could materially change the result.

One of the clearest strengths. Grands Bains thermal spa, Briançon's historic town and cultural offer, pools, ice rink, cinema, theatre, bowling and other indoor activities create a varied non-ski programme. Alti-Mag reports 45 km Nordic trails; verify against the official network map before treating this as a measured input.

A distributed evening offer across the valley, with Briançon adding town-centre bars and nightlife including a named nightclub. Current evidence does not establish high-intensity party-resort status. Existing scoring requires independent guide rankings, deduplicated venues, clubs, slope venues, events and mapped bars.

Four sectors and established settlements create a broad restaurant landscape. However, current 2026 Michelin distinctions, Gault&Millau toques and comparable mapped restaurant and specialist food-shop counts still need verification. General restaurant presence is not enough to award a high score.

value.assessment: Using the published 2026/27 Alti-Mag prices of €68/day and €345/six days, the existing large-domain v1.1 anchors (€85 to €55 day; €470 to €280 six-day) produce a provisional pass-value component of 56.7/100. This is pass value only, not total trip affordability.

mixed_ability.assessment: The published distribution spans all four grades: 15 green, 26 blue, 28 red and 13 black. Positive evidence for mixed ability, but the formula uses mapped kilometres by grade, not run counts.

access.assessment: Briançon has rail access and the valley is reachable from regional airports. No v1.1 ease score until comparable drive times, bed-to-lift distance and ski-in/ski-out share are measured.

village.assessment: Four sectors and 13 settlements create a broad village ecosystem. v1.1 village score still needs mapped food shops, groceries and village restaurants.

scoring_status.reason: The eight audience recipes have now been assessed against available resort evidence. Numeric scores require the mapped inputs used by the existing v1.1 scorer; substituting published run counts or qualitative descriptions would corrupt the method.
